features.title: Command entry point and error reporting
features.description: `node bin/todo.js` runs `main` from `src/cli.js`, which rejects a missing or unknown command with a `todo: ` message on stderr and exit 1, the one error path every later command shares.
acceptance_criteria: `node bin/todo.js` with no arguments exits 1, prints nothing on stdout, and prints one line starting with `todo: ` on stderr
`node bin/todo.js frob` exits 1, prints nothing on stdout, and prints one line starting with `todo: ` on stderr

`main(["frob"], {}, io)` from `src/cli.js`, with `io` = `{stdout(line), stderr(line)}` capturing lines, returns 1, writes no stdout line, writes one stderr line starting with `todo: `, and does not call `process.exit`

context.business: G-7, FL-5: every command shares one predictable error path, so it comes first and later commands only add handlers.
context.design: Layout per D-layout (thin `bin/todo.js` shebang entry that sets `process.exitCode` from `main`); `main(argv, env, io)` per D-cli-main; `TodoError` and the `todo: <message>` format, with unexpected exceptions reported the same way and never as a stack trace, per D-errors; strict command surface per D-commands. Tests per D-tests.

provides.F3: main(argv, env, io) command dispatch in src/cli.js and the bin/todo.js entry

features.title: JSON todo file store
features.description: `src/store.js` loads and saves the list from `TODO_FILE` (or `./todo.json`), treating a missing file as empty, rejecting corrupt files, and writing atomically.
acceptance_criteria: `load(env)` from `src/store.js`, with `env.TODO_FILE` naming a file that does not exist, returns `{nextId: 1, items: []}` and creates no file
`save(env, state)` then `load(env)` with the same `env.TODO_FILE` returns a deep-equal state, and the file content equals `JSON.stringify(state, null, 2) + "\n"`
`resolvePath({})` and `resolvePath({TODO_FILE: ""})` from `src/store.js` both return `path.resolve("todo.json")`, and `resolvePath({TODO_FILE: "x/w.json"})` returns `path.resolve("x/w.json")`
`load(env)` on a file containing `not json` throws a `TodoError` whose message includes the file path, and the file content is unchanged
`load(env)` on a file containing `[]` (valid JSON, wrong shape) throws a `TodoError` whose message includes the file path

context.business: G-6: items persist between runs; every command after F1 reads or writes this file, so storage is shared.
context.design: File shape, path resolution, missing-file and temp-file-then-rename rules per D-json-store; corrupt or wrong-shape files are `TodoError`s naming the path per D-errors (TodoError from F1). Standard library only per D-runtime. Unit tests use a fresh mkdtemp directory per D-tests.

provides.F3: load(env), save(env, state) and resolvePath(env) in src/store.js; state is {nextId, items: [{id, text, done}]}

features.title: Add an item
features.description: A user adds an item with `node bin/todo.js add <text...>`; it is stored as open and its id is printed.
acceptance_criteria: With `TODO_FILE` naming a missing file in a fresh temp directory, `node bin/todo.js add buy milk` exits 0, prints exactly `1\n` on stdout, and the file then parses to `{"nextId": 2, "items": [{"id": 1, "text": "buy milk", "done": false}]}`
A second `node bin/todo.js add eggs` against the same `TODO_FILE` exits 0 and prints exactly `2\n`

`node bin/todo.js add` with no text, and `node bin/todo.js add "   "`, each exit 1, print nothing on stdout, print a line starting with `todo: ` on stderr, and leave the file unchanged (still absent if it was absent)
`addItem(state, text)` from `src/todos.js` returns a state with a new open item whose id is the old `nextId`, and with `nextId` one higher
With `TODO_FILE` set to `<tmpA>/work.json` and the working directory `<tmpB>`, `node <repo>/bin/todo.js add x` writes the item to `<tmpA>/work.json` and creates no `<tmpB>/todo.json`

context.business: G-1, FL-1 step 1 and FL-4: capturing an item is the first thing a user does, and TODO_FILE lets them keep a list per project.
context.design: Arguments after `add` are joined with single spaces and empty-after-trim text is an error per D-commands; output is just the id per D-output; ids come from `nextId` per D-json-store; pure list logic lives in `src/todos.js` per D-layout; errors per D-errors. E2E tests spawn `process.execPath bin/todo.js` per D-tests.

provides.F4: the add command, so list tests can create items, and addItem(state, text) in src/todos.js

features.title: List open items
features.description: A user sees open items with `node bin/todo.js list`, one `<id> <text>` line each, in ascending id order.
acceptance_criteria: After `node bin/todo.js add buy milk` and `node bin/todo.js add eggs` against one `TODO_FILE`, `node bin/todo.js list` exits 0 and prints exactly `1 buy milk\n2 eggs\n`
With `TODO_FILE` naming a missing file, `node bin/todo.js list` exits 0, prints nothing, and the file still does not exist
`node bin/todo.js list extra` and `node bin/todo.js list --bogus` each exit 1, print nothing on stdout and print a line starting with `todo: ` on stderr

With `TODO_FILE` naming a file containing `not json`, `node bin/todo.js list` exits 1, prints nothing on stdout, prints a `todo: ` line on stderr that contains the file path, and leaves the file unchanged

context.business: G-2, FL-1 step 2 and FL-6: seeing what is still open is the reason to keep the list.
context.design: Output format and ascending order per D-output; extra arguments and unknown flags are errors per D-commands; read-only commands never create the file per D-json-store; errors per D-errors. Listing logic as a pure function in `src/todos.js` per D-layout.

provides.F5: the list command and a pure listing function in src/todos.js that F5 extends with --all

features.title: Mark an item done and list all items
features.description: A user marks an item done with `node bin/todo.js done <id>`; it leaves `list` and shows as `<id> [x] <text>` in `list --all`.
acceptance_criteria: After adding `a` (id 1) and `b` (id 2), `node bin/todo.js done 1` exits 0 and prints nothing, and `node bin/todo.js list` then prints exactly `2 b\n`
In that state, `node bin/todo.js list --all` exits 0 and prints exactly `1 [x] a\n2 b\n`
Running `node bin/todo.js done 1` a second time exits 0, prints nothing, and `list --all` still prints `1 [x] a` first
`node bin/todo.js done 99` (no such id) exits 1, prints nothing on stdout, prints a line starting with `todo: ` on stderr, and leaves the file byte-for-byte unchanged
`node bin/todo.js done abc`, `node bin/todo.js done 0`, `node bin/todo.js done` and `node bin/todo.js done 1 2` each exit 1, print nothing on stdout and print a line starting with `todo: ` on stderr

context.business: G-3, G-4, FL-2: finishing work is the main loop of a todo list, and `--all` lets the user see what they finished.
context.design: Id syntax `/^[1-9][0-9]*$/` and argument rules per D-commands; `[x]` after the id and silent success per D-output; re-marking is a no-op and an unknown id is an error per D-errors; the file is rewritten atomically per D-json-store. Extends F4's list command with `--all`.

provides.F6: the done command, list --all output, and id parsing and validation in src/cli.js that rm reuses

features.title: Delete an item
features.description: A user deletes an item with `node bin/todo.js rm <id>`; it appears in no listing and its id is never reused.
acceptance_criteria: After adding `a` (id 1) and `b` (id 2), `node bin/todo.js rm 2` exits 0 and prints nothing, and `node bin/todo.js list --all` then prints exactly `1 a\n`
After that `rm 2`, `node bin/todo.js add c` exits 0 and prints exactly `3\n`
`node bin/todo.js rm 99` (no such id) exits 1, prints nothing on stdout, prints a line starting with `todo: ` on stderr, and leaves the file byte-for-byte unchanged
`node bin/todo.js rm abc`, `node bin/todo.js rm` and `node bin/todo.js rm 1 2` each exit 1, print nothing on stdout and print a line starting with `todo: ` on stderr

context.business: G-5, FL-3: removing items keeps the list relevant.
context.design: Ids are never reused because `nextId` is kept per D-json-store; id and argument rules per D-commands, reusing F5's id parsing; silent success per D-output; errors per D-errors.
